name: astra-workflow
description: Route all execution to bounded workers. Root Astra High orchestrates and plans; separate Astra High specialists own architecture, original design and motion, difficult implementation and substantive review. Supporting Luna, Terra, Gemini Flash and Opus workers execute accepted decisions.
---

# Astra workflow

Apply this user-selected workflow to every root request. Explicit worker sessions execute their own role and brief, without restarting root routing. Read the relevant references once when needed. Latest user scope and project security/implementation standards remain binding.

## Roles and ownership

- Root Astra High, Standard only orchestrates and plans. It can inspect enough context to route work, clarify scope, write coordination plans/checkpoints and briefs, read status/evidence, validate review evidence and coverage, route findings and accept results. Root cannot produce implementation, configuration, product, design, source, test, research, explanation or content deliverables, run their implementation/checks or fix findings. Delegate tool-only mutations and trivial transformations too. Inline root prose is limited to status, scope, execution-plan discussion and summaries of returned evidence.
- Separate Astra High, Standard specialists execute bounded architecture/business-rule design, original visual design and motion including creative implementation, algorithm/test-strategy design, technical investigation, difficult implementation/debugging and substantive review assignments. They may make the assigned technical/design decisions. They never orchestrate or recursively delegate. Root-only execution restrictions do not apply to specialist sessions.
- Independent Astra High, Standard reviewers use a fresh read-only context. They investigate and review the assigned artifact, supply checkable findings and recheck repairs. They never implement or coordinate, and never independently review their own implementation.
- Luna Max, Fast handles clear transformations, repetitive changes, narrow implementation and specified tests.
- Terra Medium, Standard handles bounded ordinary engineering across related files using accepted behavior and existing patterns.
- Gemini 3.8 Flash Medium handles self-contained content, translation, extraction, lookup and specified checks. High handles longer context or interdependent approved cases. Both are supporting execution roles.
- Opus 4.6 Thinking through the existing Antigravity route handles harder bounded implementation, execution-evidence reconciliation and specified test matrices. Use `claude-opus-4-6-thinking` without `--effort`. It rejects that override. Thinking is the provider's mode label, not a measured reasoning budget.

Supporting workers do not choose new architecture, business rules, original design/motion or test strategy. They return those needs to root for a separate Astra specialist. Do not use Sol, new provider connections or paid API fallback. These are behavioral boundaries, not a tool-enforced firewall; child permissions are inherited.

## Use only the necessary process

Classify by uncertainty, consequence and verification cost. Start with one worker, at most two independent workers active across all roles. Shared-file edits and dependent work run sequentially.

1. Clear small requests need only a compact worker brief. No plan file or separate review by default. Requested explanations, research, translations and content transformations are delegated deliverables, including one-line requests.
2. Bounded implementation needs context, a cohesive brief, worker execution and returned evidence.
3. New architecture, original design or ambiguous behavior goes to a separate Astra specialist to inspect and develop options. Root handles material scope questions and required user direction before dependent work.
4. Complex or consequential work needs one root coordination plan with acceptance criteria and dependency-aware batches. Technical/design specifications are specialist deliverables. Add child plans only for substantial independent phases. Use an independent challenge when justified by a concrete uncertainty.

Root may use coordination tools and maintain plans/checkpoints directly. It delegates deeper code investigation, verification commands and every substantive execution artifact. Do not add planning rituals to simple requests. Necessary persistent project artifacts belong in `.hyperflow/`; projectless intermediates use `work/` and deliverables use `outputs/`.

## Quality and delegation

Apply Unslop and Humanizer together to authored prose. Apply the installed Code Simplifier guidance to changed code before verification, within the assigned role. Read [quality.md](references/quality.md) for the source paths and code, architecture and testing requirements. The specialist derives algorithm/scale constraints and relevant test cases; supporting workers execute accepted decisions and report new risks. Root checks evidence coverage and assigns gaps, rather than doing the investigation itself.

Read [briefs-and-tests.md](references/briefs-and-tests.md) when writing execution or testing briefs. Specify outcome, boundaries, accepted decisions, expected results, applicable failure cases, commands and returned evidence. Specialists may design decisions within their assigned scope; supporting workers may not. Every worker has no recursive delegation. Ordinary briefs do not authorize commits, push, publication, deployment or messages to others.

User-authorized integration/release remains possible through a separate explicit bounded execution assignment. Root names the action, target/revision, allowed paths, required gates and existing authorization. The worker may execute only that action after the gates pass. Root never runs release commands itself. Reviewers always remain read-only.

## Dispatch

Read [dispatch.md](references/dispatch.md). Exact named presets are `astra_specialist`, `astra_reviewer`, `astra_luna` and `astra_terra`. A specialist uses `astra-specialist` CLI profile through runner lane `astra-specialist` when the native client cannot establish the complete preset. A reviewer uses the separate read-only `astra-review` CLI profile.

Native Luna model/effort selection alone does not establish Fast speed; use the runner when Fast cannot be verified. Native Astra/Terra selection is valid only with verified High/Medium effort respectively and Standard speed. Never silently downgrade required settings. Gemini Flash and Opus use the existing installed `agy` relay with exact per-run model/effort settings.

## Verification, review validation and repair

Worker success means ready for review, never automatic acceptance. Workers return artifacts/changed paths, criteria completed, commands/results and unresolved cases. Root validates evidence and coverage. A substantive review or deeper investigation goes to a separate Astra specialist; consequential correctness, security, architecture and migrations require independent Astra review. Ordinary work may rely on adequate targeted worker checks and root evidence validation.

Root validates every finding against the current revision, requirements, supplied reproduction/evidence, severity and scope. Mark it confirmed, rejected with reason or needs evidence. Check clean-review coverage too. Missing reproduction or substantive investigation goes back to the reviewer or a designated Astra specialist. Send confirmed issues to the responsible implementation worker, preferably its existing session, with IDs, locations, expected behavior, allowed scope and closure checks. Architecture/design fixes go to the responsible Astra specialist. Reviewers do not implement findings.

Give the responsible worker one targeted repair round per batch. Workers run verification; the independent reviewer rechecks repairs when one was used. Root validates returned repair and follow-up review evidence before closing each finding. Unresolved confirmed in-scope issues prevent acceptance. Record finding ID, reviewed revision, evidence, validation status, owner, fix revision and verification result in an existing substantive task artifact; small work only needs a concise repair brief. Review-only scope remains read-only unless implementation is authorized.

Prefer compaction at 60% of verified effective active context, within 50-70%. Read [compaction.md](references/compaction.md) for installed per-model thresholds, checkpoint preservation and provider limits. Keep the native summarization prompt. Context handoffs preserve ownership, review/repair evidence, attempt history and sticky Codex-only restrictions.

Read [recovery.md](references/recovery.md) for multi-stage work, interruptions or failures. Automatic supporting fallback remains authorized after provider failure or one unsuccessful targeted repair. Normal initial routing may use Flash or Opus through Antigravity. Failure/unavailability of either option immediately makes the remaining affected task/batch chain Codex-only: Flash prefers eligible Luna Max/Fast then Terra Medium/Standard; Opus prefers eligible Terra then Luna. Initial validated review findings still get one targeted repair with their owner; actual Antigravity provider/process failure, confirmed unavailability or unsuccessful repair triggers immediate handoff without another Antigravity retry. The live root performs reassignment after stopped-state/partial-work evidence is reconciled. Deeper reconciliation investigation is delegated. The runner executes one attempt; it does not rotate models or accept results.

Astra roles never fall back to cheaper models. An Astra specialist/reviewer process or session failure permits at most one fresh same-Astra High/Standard session per batch after stopped-state reconciliation and evidence of service availability. Astra service unavailability pauses affected work. Unresolved work after an Astra specialist's targeted repair pauses for a revised plan or user input, never support-model fallback. Root Astra unavailability pauses the entire workflow, requests worker cancellation and preserves the last verified checkpoint. Resume only after reconciling unknown results.

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { BUILD_TIMEOUT, type CommandResult } from './combination-helpers.js';

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const REGISTER = require.resolve('ts-node/register');

const CHECK_FEATURES = `
  const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
  const { AuthFeaturesService } = require('./src/auth/services/auth-features.service');
  const { AuthFeature } = require('./src/auth/enums/auth-feature.enum');
  const selected = new Set(JSON.parse(process.argv[1]));
  const features = [
    [AuthFeature.PASSWORD, 'email-password'],
    [AuthFeature.MAGIC_LINK, 'magic-link'],
    [AuthFeature.TWO_FACTOR, 'totp'],
    [AuthFeature.PASSKEYS, 'passkeys'],
  ];
  for (const enabled of [true, false]) {
    const service = new AuthFeaturesService({ get: () => enabled });
    for (const [feature, id] of features) {
      const expected = enabled && selected.has(id);
      assert.equal(service.isEnabled(feature), expected, id);
      if (expected) service.assertEnabled(feature);
      else assert.throws(() => service.assertEnabled(feature), { status: 404 });
    }
  }
`;

/** A configured runtime flag must never restore a method the CLI removed. */
export function verifyFeatureAvailability(project: string, features: string[]): CommandResult {
  const result = spawnSync(
    process.execPath,
    ['-r', REGISTER, '-e', CHECK_FEATURES, JSON.stringify(features)],
    { cwd: join(project, 'backend'), encoding: 'utf8', timeout: BUILD_TIMEOUT },
  );
  return { ok: result.status === 0, output: `${result.stdout ?? ''}${result.stderr ?? ''}` };
}
